morbi.headline: Morbi faces severe export contraction alongside recurring domestic trade credit defaults and fraud.
what_changed: India's ceramic tile export volumes plunged 46% during April-July 2026, leading to a weak full-year FY27 export outlook.
Multiple buyer fraud incidents emerged, exposing manufacturers to unsecured trade credit defaults in the domestic market.
stress_signals: Export volumes dropped 46% year-on-year in Apr-Jul 2026, severely dampening the FY27 demand outlook for ceramic tile makers [434975bd08e0].
A Mumbai-based buyer allegedly defrauded a Morbi ceramic unit of Rs 44 lakh after procuring tiles on credit [e694c857f915].
A buyer absconded after securing 7,865 ceramic tile boxes on credit, reflecting recurring unsecured payment defaults in the cluster [76fdd3301f32].
what_to_watch: Full-year FY27 export trajectory and subsequent export volume prints following the 46% drop in Apr-Jul 2026.
Elongation of debtor collection cycles and rising non-payment/fraud risks on unsecured domestic credit sales.
Working capital utilization and cash flow stress in export-focused tile manufacturing units facing volume drops.

surat.headline: Surat faces severe yarn cost shocks, labor unrest, and embroidery and diamond export stress.
what_changed: Surat weaving and loom units face impending Diwali shutdowns driven by a 45-50% raw material/yarn price surge (up ₹50/kg), impacting up to 75,000 workers.
Labor unrest escalated across textile and embroidery segments, resulting in strikes, migrant worker departures to UP/Bihar, over 80 worker detentions, and union disputes.
Embroidery units remain locked in a three-month operational deadlock, while diamond exporters face a 7% drop in polished shipments alongside UK regulatory scrutiny on lab-grown ads.
Policy support surfaced with the GST Council granting ITC refunds and easing highway checks, while a new textile policy is slated within three months.
stress_signals: Input cost surge: Looms face early 15-day to month-long shutdowns due to ₹50/kg yarn price increases and a 45-50% raw material cost spike [48c63a4e50b6, b567711c9ed4, 1b54f570ed7b].

Labor disruptions: Widespread protests over hours, holidays, and wages led to an exodus of migrant workers, job walkouts, and the detention of over 80 embroidery workers [a57d83616799, 7697e96a190e, af8a29b318b7, d6a4b0e6a74b].

Segment-specific liquidity and credit stress: A three-month impasse persists in embroidery, individual trade defaults surfaced (₹29.57 lakh grey fabric and ₹70,000 polishing wages), and an arrest occurred in a ₹10.14 crore fraud case [29331b975c9e, 698c779932f2, e7921383cbb7, 2514ad7d6e20, c4997bb35d98].

External and operational headwinds: Polished diamond exports dropped 7%, UK authorities launched crackdowns on LGD advertising, and eight-hour power cuts hit continuous operations [167f80ff6cdc, 975918f112f3, b1b313249339].
improvement_signals: Regulatory easing: GST Council granted Input Tax Credit (ITC) refunds and reduced highway inspections for Surat textiles [17f0a015a73c].

Structural expansion and retail demand: Cluster units are entering defence technical textiles, MANTRA-trained entrepreneurs reached ₹120 crore in business, and bridal demand shifted to larger lab-grown diamonds [0f163b499572, 694aea903d0a, 7dc3005e0b28].
what_to_watch: Loom inventory holding and working capital utilization: Track whether prolonged closures extend past Diwali as yarn prices remain elevated.
Embroidery unit debt service: Monitor machine-loan repayment regularities and job-work receivables as the sector impasse passes the three-month mark.
Details of the forthcoming Textile Policy: Watch for specific power tariff concessions, capital subsidies, and operational release dates within the next three months [7cb0d1c51743, a3db8ea1103a].
